apariciones.subtitulo: Distancing a claim without hiding behind it

mision.consigna: Write a short news analysis of a story that spread fast before anyone checked it — invented or generic, no real names or dates.
requisitos: three different impersonal reporting patterns (*it is believed that*, *is said to*, *it remains to be seen whether*)
one sentence where you deliberately do NOT distance, because the fact is verified — and say why
use *headline*, *source* and *public opinion*
one sentence explaining how *fake news* differs from an honest error

microtareas.texto: Take three headlines from today and rewrite each with *it is claimed that* or *is reported to*. Which one got weaker, which got more honest?
Write five sentences with *is thought to have* + past participle about events whose *source* you haven't verified.
Record 90 seconds: how *public opinion* forms before the facts are in. Use at least two impersonal passives.

apariciones.subtitulo: Putting the weight where you want it in everyday talk

mision.consigna: Describe your real kitchen habits to someone who thinks you cook more than you do.
requisitos: one negative inversion (*Rarely do I…*, *Not until… did I…*)
two *what*-clefts (*What I actually eat is…*)
one *it*-cleft correcting an assumption
use *leftovers*, *a go-to recipe* and *to throw something together*

microtareas.texto: Write your *go-to recipe* in three sentences, then rewrite the last one as a *what*-cleft.
Five sentences starting with *Rarely*, *Never*, *Only when*, *Not until*, *Little did I*. All about food.
Record 90 seconds: are you a *fussy eater* or do you have a *sweet tooth*? Two clefts minimum.

apariciones.subtitulo: The verb that belongs to the noun

mision.consigna: Write the email you'd send a financial adviser explaining your situation and what you want from a first meeting.
requisitos: six verb+noun collocations from the reference box, none repeated
*draw a distinction* between two of your goals
use *savings account*, *a rainy-day fund* and *to live within your means*
no *make* or *do* with an abstract noun

microtareas.texto: List ten nouns about money you use at work or at home. Write the verb each one really takes.
Fix these in your head: *raise a concern*, *meet a requirement*, *bear the cost*. One sentence each about your *rainy-day fund*.
Record 90 seconds about *financial independence* in your country. Count the collocations afterwards.

apariciones.subtitulo: Disagreeing with a sales pitch you half believe

mision.consigna: A friend is about to splash out on something expensive because it's on special offer. Talk them out of it without making them feel stupid.
requisitos: four different disagreement formulas from the reference box
one *Yes, and the difficulty is…* that accepts their point first
use *special offer*, *a false economy* and *warranty*
never start a sentence with *No* or *But*

microtareas.texto: Write down the last *purchase decision* you regret. What argument would have stopped you?
Rewrite three blunt objections (*That's a waste of money*) as *Help me understand how…* questions.
Record 90 seconds disagreeing with: *Buying cheap is always the smart choice.* Use *to shop on impulse*.

apariciones.subtitulo: Cutting who and which out of your descriptions

mision.consigna: Write a profile of a hobby you've tried, for a club newsletter aimed at complete beginners.
requisitos: five reduced relatives or participle clauses
one *having* + past participle opening
at least one case where you keep the full relative on purpose, because the pronoun is an object
use *spare time*, *to take up a hobby* and *to get the hang of something*

microtareas.texto: Write five sentences with *who is / which was*, then cut them down. Which ones can't be cut?
Describe people at your gym or club: *anyone taking…*, *the ones given…*. Five lines.
Record 90 seconds: what helps you *unwind* after work? Use two participle clauses.

apariciones.subtitulo: No very, no thing, no get — at the counter

mision.consigna: Write a complaint-free account of a recent dealing with an office or a service provider, as if for a friend who's about to do the same.
requisitos: none of the banned words: *very, good, bad, thing, a lot, nice, interesting, make, get, big*
three precise adjectives you had to search for
use *red tape*, *customer service* and *to fill in the form*
one sentence with *to be sent from pillar to post*

microtareas.texto: Take a real email you wrote this week. Circle every banned word and replace it.
Describe the last time you *got put on hold* in five sentences — no *very*, no *bad*.
Record 90 seconds on *red tape* in your country. Replay it and count the banned words.

apariciones.subtitulo: Health advice with the conclusion up front

mision.consigna: Summarise a health article, podcast or doctor's advice you received, for a colleague who's *running themselves into the ground*.
requisitos: conclusion in the first two sentences
exactly three supports
one declared omission (*I'm skipping X*)
use *wellbeing*, *to recover* and *to listen to your body*

microtareas.texto: Summarise something you read about sleep or stress in exactly 50 words.
Same text, 15 words. What had to go?
Record 90 seconds: what does *staying fit* really require? Start with *The short version is…*.

apariciones.subtitulo: An opinion on learning with a reason and a limit

mision.consigna: Give your honest view on whether employers should pay for *continuing education* that doesn't relate to the job.
requisitos: a stated position, a reason that isn't a restatement, and an acknowledged limit
one distinction (*I'd separate two things…*)
one question that invites the other person's view
use *career path*, *continuing education* and *to keep up to date*

microtareas.texto: Write your opinion on *continuing education* in one line. Underneath, the reason. Underneath, where you'd stop short.
Ask someone *Where do you land on…?* about *on-the-job training* at work. Write down their answer.
Record 90 seconds: *Is a degree still the best start to a career path?* End with a limit.

apariciones.subtitulo: Getting a yes on a green measure from someone who doesn't care

mision.consigna: Persuade a sceptical neighbour or colleague to support a concrete measure that reduces your building's or office's *carbon footprint*.
requisitos: two conditional offers (*If you could… I'd be able to…*)
one reframe from their position to their interest
one *What would it take?*
use *carbon footprint*, *greenhouse gases* and *biodiversity*

microtareas.texto: Write the measure you'd propose, then the three interests someone might have against it.
Three conditional concessions that give nothing unless the other side moves.
Record 90 seconds making the case on *climate change* to someone who cares only about cost.

apariciones.subtitulo: Weighing two kinds of family

mision.consigna: Compare the family culture you grew up in with one you've seen up close in another country or household.
requisitos: one *similar in X, though not in Y*
one *Where they really diverge is…*
a conclusion with *on balance*, qualified
use *a close-knit family*, *shared values* and *to grow apart*

microtareas.texto: List three things two families you know have in common and three where they differ.
Write two sentences with *It's less a question of X and more one of Y* about *being there for someone*.
Record 90 seconds: is it easier to *fall out* with family or with friends? Weigh, don't declare.

apariciones.subtitulo: Reporting what a tech company said, and how far you believe it

mision.consigna: Write a short report on a (fictional) announcement by an app company about how it handles your data.
requisitos: three reporting verbs chosen for their connotation (*claimed*, *insisted*, *admitted*)
correct backshift in at least four clauses
one hedge adverb (*reportedly*, *allegedly*)
use *algorithm*, *data protection* and *to be hooked on an app*

microtareas.texto: Write three things an app told you in its terms, in reported speech with backshift.
Same three, now with a reporting verb that shows your doubt.
Record 90 seconds on falling down *a rabbit hole* online, reporting what a friend told you about it.

apariciones.subtitulo: A trip story built for the turn

mision.consigna: Tell the story of a moment abroad when a local custom caught you completely off guard.
requisitos: an opening that withholds the point
a clearly marked turning point (*That's when it hit me…*)
a closing line that generalises beyond the event
use *culture shock*, *to settle in* and *local custom*

microtareas.texto: Write the last line of the story first. Then the first line — one that hides it.
Write the turning point three ways. Keep the one with the most tension.
Record 90 seconds of the whole story. Did you give away the ending too early?

apariciones.subtitulo: Holding the floor while you think in a meeting

mision.consigna: Describe a meeting where you had to explain your new role to people who expected someone else.
requisitos: two ways of getting the turn
one repair when you lose the thread (*Let me start that again*)
one hand-over question
use *a steep learning curve*, *to be up to speed* and *workload*

microtareas.texto: Write three openings for jumping into a conversation that's moving fast.
Say out loud, without notes, what you *took on* in your last role. When you stall, use *Bear with me*.
Record 90 seconds: how did you *land a job* you wanted? Hand the turn over at the end.

apariciones.subtitulo: Dense writing about the housing market

mision.consigna: Write a paragraph for a report on the housing situation in a city you know.
requisitos: two reduced relatives
one participle clause
two nominalisations replacing a full clause (*the landlord's decision to…*)
use *the housing market*, *a tenancy agreement* and *utility costs*

microtareas.texto: Take three full sentences about renting and compress them into one.
Turn five verbs about *a viewing* into nouns and use each in a phrase.
Rewrite a paragraph you wrote at B2 level about being *priced out* with all three devices.

apariciones.subtitulo: Feedback on someone's cooking — behaviour, not character

mision.consigna: A friend asked for honest feedback on a dinner they cooked for you. Give it.
requisitos: describe behaviour and effect, not character
*two things worked, one didn't*
one line acknowledging missing context
use *ingredient*, *to season* and *local and seasonal*

microtareas.texto: Write two feedback sentences about a meal: one about the cook, one about what happened on the plate. Keep the second.
Rewrite *You always overdo the salt* as behaviour + impact.
Record 90 seconds giving feedback on a *balanced diet* someone is trying. End with *How do you want to handle it?*

apariciones.subtitulo: Regret after a faux pas abroad

mision.consigna: Recount a *faux pas* you made (or nearly made) while travelling and what you would do differently.
requisitos: one *I wish I'd…*
two modal perfects (*could have*, *should have*)
one third conditional that runs into the present
use *a faux pas*, *to acclimatise* and *local custom*

microtareas.texto: Write three *I wish I'd known…* sentences about a trip.
Turn them into a chain: wish → should have → if I'd…
Record 90 seconds on *mass tourism*: what should cities have done differently?

apariciones.subtitulo: Complaining about the office without complaining

mision.consigna: Describe a manager who micromanages to a colleague, using only understatement.
requisitos: four understatement formulas
no word stronger than *a bit of a…*
one ironic *not bad* that actually means bad
use *to micromanage*, *to pull your weight* and *workload*

microtareas.texto: Write three blunt complaints about work, then rewrite each as understatement.
Explain in writing why *That could have gone better* can be harsher than *It went badly*.
Record 90 seconds about a *promotion* you didn't get, understated throughout.

apariciones.subtitulo: Only, even, just — where they sit at the counter

mision.consigna: Write instructions for a newcomer on how to deal with a local registration office.
requisitos: *only* in three positions with three meanings
one *even*
one *just* in the perfect
use *to fill in the form*, *red tape* and *customer service*

microtareas.texto: Write *I only need a copy of the form* and move *only* four times. Note what changes.
Five sentences about *a helpline* using *even* in different positions.
Record 90 seconds explaining who you would ask *to escalate a complaint* at an office you've been to.

apariciones.subtitulo: Walking a listener through a buying decision

mision.consigna: Talk someone through how you decide on a big purchase, from first idea to buying.
requisitos: a spoken turn of at least two minutes
*Let me take those in turn* to announce the structure
one marked digression (*Just as an aside*) and a return
use *to shop around*, *warranty* and *a hard sell*

microtareas.texto: Write the five markers you'll use and where they go.
Say your *purchase decision* process out loud with no markers. Then with them.
Record 2 minutes on whether *haggling over the price* is acceptable where you live. End with *The upshot is*.

apariciones.subtitulo: A complaint to a club that keeps letting you down

mision.consigna: Write to a club or course you joined about a problem that's now happened twice.
requisitos: facts, effect, specific request — in that order
one firm escalation line
a closing formula that keeps the door open
use *to join a club*, *to make time for something* and *to be a regular somewhere*

microtareas.texto: Write the facts of your complaint in three sentences. No adjectives.
Now the effect: why it matters to someone trying to *take up a hobby*.
Record 90 seconds making the complaint by phone. Stay on the problem.

apariciones.subtitulo: Advice that hands the decision back

mision.consigna: A friend asks what to do about a relative who keeps crossing their boundaries.
requisitos: three options, framed as options
one *What worked for me was…*
hand the decision back explicitly
use *to set boundaries*, *to walk on eggshells* and *to see eye to eye*

microtareas.texto: Rewrite three *you should* sentences as options.
Write what worked for you with someone you had to *forgive*.
Record 90 seconds giving advice on *shared values* in a relationship. End with *But that's your call*.

apariciones.subtitulo: An environmental argument with three kinds of emphasis

mision.consigna: Write an opinion column arguing that we underestimate how close some *tipping points* are.
requisitos: one negative inversion
one *it*-cleft and one *what*-cleft
one fronted phrase (*That much we can agree on*)
use *tipping point*, *drought* and *greenhouse gases*

microtareas.texto: Write one plain paragraph about *carbon footprint*. Then mark where each device could go.
Rewrite it using all three devices, one per sentence, not stacked.
Record 90 seconds: what surprised you most about *drought*? Start with *What struck me…*

apariciones.subtitulo: A chain of speculation about your own money

mision.consigna: Predict where your finances will be in five years, as if explaining it to a partner.
requisitos: an observation, a graded prediction and what could prove you wrong
three different degrees of likelihood
*If current trends hold…*
use *savings buffer*, *investment strategy* and *financial independence*

microtareas.texto: Write three predictions about interest rates, from *bound to* to *wouldn't surprise me*.
For each, write what would prove you wrong.
Record 90 seconds on whether a *savings account* is still worth it.

apariciones.subtitulo: Hedging a health claim so it survives

mision.consigna: Explain to a friend why you think preventive check-ups matter, without overstating the evidence.
requisitos: four different hedging devices (modal, adverb, reporting, impersonal)
one *up to a point*
no claim stronger than your evidence
use *preventive check-up*, *wellbeing* and *to recover*

microtareas.texto: Write three health claims you believe. Hedge each exactly as far as your evidence goes.
Find a claim online about *staying fit* and rewrite it honestly hedged.
Record 90 seconds: *Does exercise speed up how you recover from illness?* Hedge everything.

apariciones.subtitulo: Reconstructing what happened to a neighbourhood

mision.consigna: Explain how a neighbourhood you know changed, reasoning from the evidence you can see today.
requisitos: a chain from strong certainty (*must have*) to a dismissed possibility (*can't have*)
one *should have… but clearly didn't*
a closing *The most likely explanation is…*
use *to move house*, *transport links* and *utility costs*

microtareas.texto: List three things you noticed in a street that changed. Write a *must have* for each.
Add a *might have… though* and a *can't have* to the chain.
Record 90 seconds on how *a tenancy agreement* in your city must have changed.

apariciones.subtitulo: One idiom per paragraph about learning

mision.consigna: Write a short post about how you keep up to date in your field.
requisitos: three idioms, one per paragraph, never two in a row
each checked for register
one sentence explaining why you avoided a textbook idiom
use *to keep up to date*, *career path* and *continuing education*

microtareas.texto: Pick three idioms from the reference box and write where each fits and where it would sound wrong.
Write about *exam anxiety* using *as a last resort* naturally.
Record 90 seconds on your *career path*. One idiom only — make it count.

apariciones.subtitulo: The careful report on automation

mision.consigna: Write the conclusions section of a report on automating a task in your team.
requisitos: three hedges, two agentless passives and one impersonal reporting frame
at least one sentence fusing all three
one claim you leave unhedged, and why
use *to automate a task*, *to keep a human in the loop* and *biased*

microtareas.texto: Write three blunt sentences about *algorithms* at work. Hedge and depersonalise each.
Write two sentences with *It has been suggested that…* about being *made redundant*.
Record 90 seconds explaining *data protection* risks like a cautious consultant.

apariciones.subtitulo: Disagreeing about a news story with someone who trusts it

mision.consigna: Someone shares a headline you think is misleading. Disagree with them publicly, in a group chat or meeting.
requisitos: challenge the source, not the person
one *That's true of X, less so of Y*
one move that leaves their position somewhere to stand
use *headline*, *credibility* and *media literacy*

microtareas.texto: Write the assumption behind a headline you disagree with.
Three ways of saying *That's fake news* without saying it.
Record 90 seconds disagreeing with: *If many outlets report it, it's true.*

apariciones.subtitulo: Choosing the rung on the register ladder

mision.consigna: Write two versions of the same message about getting your foreign qualifications recognised: one to a friend, one to the authority.
requisitos: three phrasal/Latinate/collocation triples used appropriately
no Latinate verb in the friend version where a phrasal fits
no phrasal verb in the formal version where it would be too casual
use *continuing professional development*, *a refresher course* and *to top up your qualifications*

microtareas.texto: Write the ladder for *look into*, *find out* and *sort out*.
Tell a friend about *a refresher course* you're planning, all phrasal.
Record 90 seconds explaining *continuing professional development* formally, then informally.

apariciones.subtitulo: Summarising culture shock for someone about to move

mision.consigna: Summarise what you've learned about adapting to a new country for someone moving next month.
requisitos: top-down: conclusion, three supports, caveat
one sentence saying what you left out and why
one *Treat that as directional*
use *a sense of belonging*, *cultural baggage* and *to acclimatise*

microtareas.texto: Write your advice as one sentence. Then three supports.
Say what you'd leave out about *romanticising a place*.
Record 90 seconds: *If you only remember one thing about culture shock…*

apariciones.subtitulo: Comparing two ways of getting better

mision.consigna: Compare rest and active recovery after an illness or injury, for someone who's recovering now.
requisitos: weigh the two, don't rank them flatly
one *but only just*
one *It's less a question of X and more one of Y*
use *chronic / acute*, *recovery* and *side effect*

microtareas.texto: List what *taking it easy* and staying active have in common.
Write where they diverge for *chronic* versus *acute* problems.
Record 90 seconds comparing two treatments you know about, weighted.

apariciones.subtitulo: An opinion about bureaucracy that holds up

mision.consigna: Give your view on whether public offices should keep fixed office hours or move entirely online.
requisitos: position, reason, limit
one *That's my instinct, not my evidence*
one question inviting a different experience
use *office hours*, *caseworker* and *delay*

microtareas.texto: Write your position on *office hours* and the one fact that would change your mind.
Ask someone how they'd *file an objection* and what they think of the process.
Record 90 seconds: *Is paperwork the price of fairness?*

apariciones.subtitulo: Negotiating a menu with conflicting needs

mision.consigna: Negotiate a shared dinner plan with someone who has a *food intolerance* and someone who hates *food waste*.
requisitos: two conditional offers
one *My constraint is…*
one concession that asks for something back
use *food intolerance*, *food waste* and *comfort food*

microtareas.texto: Write the interest behind each person's position.
Draft three *Would it help if…* proposals.
Record 90 seconds persuading someone to try a dish you had *to acquire a taste for*.

apariciones.subtitulo: Gerund or infinitive when the meaning moves

mision.consigna: Write a short piece on a feature an app rolled out that you regret agreeing to.
requisitos: *regret* with both forms, meaning different things
*go on* with both forms
one perfect gerund (*Having…*)
use *to roll out a feature*, *to opt out* and *black box*

microtareas.texto: Write *I regret to say* and *I regret saying* sentences about an *algorithm*.
Two sentences with *meant to* and *means -ing* about *data protection*.
Record 90 seconds: what did you mean to change in your settings and never did?

apariciones.subtitulo: Steering a group discussion on net zero

mision.consigna: Summarise how you'd chair a short discussion on whether your town should aim for *net zero*.
requisitos: two ways of taking the turn back when it drifts
one *It depends what you mean by…*
one closing hand-over
use *net zero*, *renewable energy* and *circular economy*

microtareas.texto: Write three ways to bring a digression back to the point.
Explain *circular economy* out loud; if you stall, repair and continue.
Record 90 seconds on what *sustainable* means to you, handing over at the end.

apariciones.subtitulo: The move that didn't go to plan

mision.consigna: Tell the story of a move you made — or nearly made — and what the new place taught you.
requisitos: an opening that withholds the outcome
a turning point marked with *out of nowhere* or *I never saw it coming*
a closing line looking back
use *to move house*, *utility costs* and *transport links*

microtareas.texto: Write the least expected moment of a move you made.
Write the ending line that generalises from it.
Record 90 seconds: what did you learn from a *housing cooperative* or shared building?

apariciones.subtitulo: Regret about money decisions

mision.consigna: Write about a financial decision you'd make differently now, and what it has cost you.
requisitos: unreal past, modal perfect and third conditional blended in one paragraph
one mixed conditional reaching into the present
one *In hindsight*
use *the state pension*, *a workplace pension* and *to pay into a pension*

microtareas.texto: Three *I wish I'd…* sentences about *paying into a pension* earlier.
Turn the strongest one into *If I'd…, I would now…*.
Record 90 seconds on *a workplace pension* you should have joined sooner.

apariciones.subtitulo: Compressing a status update for a busy manager

mision.consigna: Write a three-paragraph status update about a project where you are *spread too thin*.
requisitos: two reduced relatives and two participle clauses
three nominalisations
no sentence longer than 30 words
use *workload*, *to push back on something* and *personal responsibility*

microtareas.texto: Write your *workload* in full sentences, then compress it into one.
Turn *I decided to push back on the deadline* into a noun phrase.
Rewrite an old email of yours to your *manager* with all three devices.

apariciones.subtitulo: Feedback on a practice routine that's stopped working

mision.consigna: Give feedback to a friend whose training for a hobby has *plateaued*.
requisitos: behaviour and impact, never character
one thing to keep, one to change
one question that lets them respond
use *deliberate practice*, *to hone a skill* and *to plateau*

microtareas.texto: Write two feedback lines on your own practice, as if about someone else.
Rewrite *You're lazy about it* as behaviour + impact.
Record 90 seconds on *making time for* practice. End with *What's your read?*

apariciones.subtitulo: Complaining to a news outlet

mision.consigna: Write to an outlet about a story you think was framed misleadingly.
requisitos: facts, effect, specific request
*This is the second time I've had to raise this*
no attack on the journalist as a person
use *to frame a story*, *credibility* and *an echo chamber*

microtareas.texto: Summarise the story and what the *headline* implied, in three lines.
Write the specific request you'd make.
Record 90 seconds on why you *take* some outlets *with a pinch of salt*.

apariciones.subtitulo: The preposition that changes the meaning

mision.consigna: Write a reflective paragraph about a rift in a family or friendship and what it rested on.
requisitos: *consist in* vs *consist of*
*concerned with* vs *concerned about*
*result from* and *result in* in the same paragraph
use *estrangement*, *disappointment* and *to forgive someone*

microtareas.texto: Two sentences on *estrangement*: one with *result from*, one with *result in*.
Write what *shared values* consist in, then what a family consists of.
Record 90 seconds on *disappointment* and what it rested on.

apariciones.subtitulo: The word that makes the product sound good or bad

mision.consigna: Write two reviews of the same product: one by a fan, one by a sceptic, using near-synonyms that shift connotation.
requisitos: four near-synonym pairs with opposite connotation
one *It comes across as…*
one *That's putting it kindly*
use *ethical sourcing*, *supply chain* and *a hard sell*

microtareas.texto: Write five neutral words about shops, then a positive and negative near-synonym for each.
Describe someone who *haggles over the price*: frugal or stingy? Both versions.
Record 90 seconds on *consumer protection*, choosing every adjective deliberately.

apariciones.subtitulo: No investigate, no tolerate — phrasal verbs for your hobby

mision.consigna: Tell the story of how a hobby started, grew and maybe turned into something more.
requisitos: six phrasal verbs from the reference box
no Latinate synonym where a phrasal fits
one *end up -ing*
use *a side hustle*, *to plateau* and *to turn a hobby into a job*

microtareas.texto: Write five sentences with Latinate verbs about your hobby, then swap each for a phrasal.
Write about something you *put off* and later *took back up*.
Record 90 seconds: does money *take the fun out of* a hobby?

apariciones.subtitulo: Speculating about who is accountable when AI decides

mision.consigna: Speculate on how AI decisions at work will be regulated within ten years.
requisitos: an observation, a graded prediction, and what would prove you wrong
three different degrees of certainty
one explicit *That said, a lot could change*
use *accountability*, *informed consent* and *to displace workers*

microtareas.texto: Write three predictions about *black box* systems at different strengths.
For each, write the fact that would make you revise it.
Record 90 seconds: will people be able to *opt out*? Graded throughout.

apariciones.subtitulo: Advice on buying less, without preaching

mision.consigna: A friend wants to stop feeling guilty about shopping. Advise them.
requisitos: options, not instructions
one *For what it's worth, I'd…*
hand the choice back
use *planned obsolescence*, *conspicuous consumption* and *the circular economy*

microtareas.texto: Write the advice you'd give yourself about *conspicuous consumption*, as options.
Rewrite *You shouldn't buy fast fashion* in three softer, still honest forms.
Record 90 seconds on *consumer protection* and *planned obsolescence*. End with *But that's your call*.

apariciones.subtitulo: Emphasis in writing about food and memory

mision.consigna: Write about a dish that carries your family's *culinary heritage*.
requisitos: one negative inversion, one cleft and one fronting — in different sentences
no device used twice
one sentence plain on purpose, for contrast
use *culinary heritage*, *to pass down a recipe* and *conviviality*

microtareas.texto: Write the story of a recipe plainly. Mark the one sentence that deserves emphasis.
Give it three emphatic versions and keep the best.
Record 90 seconds on *comfort food*. Start with *It was… that…*

apariciones.subtitulo: One money situation, three registers

mision.consigna: Write about going into the red three times: a text to a friend, an email to your bank, a formal letter disputing a fee.
requisitos: three texts with no register leak between them
at least two formal markers from the reference box in the letter
